gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured cellular data figure for any candidate. Outdoor Tech Lab logged 2.7 GB in 90 days on Verizon LTE with the Reolink Go PT Ultra: 847 motion events, about 30 MB a day or about 0.9 GB a month, with phone alerts arriving 8–12 s after motion. The rival pages give only maker estimates (eufy about 700 MB a month, Reolink 1–3 GB).
standout_why: I compared against homesecurityradar.com (data-cost guide, cited, and the no-Wi-Fi guide), buffaloalarm.com (cited), smarthomeexplorer.com and securitycamlab.com. Home Security Radar and Buffalo Alarm both say they do no hands-on testing and give only maker data estimates. Securitycamlab gives a vendor 1–3 GB/month estimate and nothing measured. Smarthomeexplorer does use Outdoor Tech Lab's Go PT Ultra test, but only for uptime, the 34.6% false-positive rate and night range. It says data use and alert latency are not reported. No rival page states measured data use, alert latency or live-view start time for any camera.
decides: This confirms that the Reolink Go PT Ultra (sold as Go Series G440, the card ChatGPT called 'best overall') has a published 90-day cellular-only winter test. That test supports a 1 GB/month plan for about 28 events a day and shows the 21.6 Wh battery holding at or above 85% on solar in December. It can't settle Reolink against eufy S330 or Arenti GO3G on data or latency, because no named reviewer has published those figures for the other two. For eufy, the only figures are maker estimates or eufy's own customer anecdote. Fstoppers' woodland test is a counterweight: the stock panel couldn't keep up under tree cover, so the solar result depends on how open the site is.

unsourced: Arenti GO3G: I searched for a named reviewer or lab measuring data use, battery drain, alert latency or night range and found only retailer listings, manuals and anonymous buyer comments.

eufy 4G LTE Cam S330: I looked for an independently measured monthly cellular data figure, alert latency or live-view time. GearBrain (Mark Westlake, 2025-01-28) tested it for three months but on dual-band Wi-Fi and published no figures. Its 700 MB/month is eufy's estimate. I couldn't open the Tom's Guide review or its 7-month follow-up to check for winter battery or data figures.
Arlo Go 2: I looked for measured data use or latency on LTE only and found none. Mighty Gadget's battery figure is mainly on Wi-Fi.
Reolink Go PT Plus: I didn't search for named measurements because I ran out of tool calls.
Reolink Go Series G440 = Go PT Ultra: retailers and B&H's product title ('Go PT Ultra G440') link the two names, but I didn't find a Reolink statement saying they're the same camera.
